content.thinking: Since there's essentially no data for this incident, I need to write the postmortem honestly stating the root cause is unknown rather than fabricating numbers or durations. I'll structure it with root_cause, executive_summary, and an optional assumptions array, being careful not to invent measurements or restate given figures as if I computed them myself—though I can reference the alert time.

assumptions: Assumed the alert itself was genuine; with no metrics retrieved, we could not confirm or rule out that the alert was spurious.
Assumed the fault was ongoing at the end of the available data, because no recovery was observed — absence of a recovery signal is not proof the service was still broken.
Assumed the absence of recent feature-flag changes is accurate as reported by the flag provider; no independent check was made.
Assumed customers were affected in some way, since an error-rate alert implies failed requests, but the scope, volume and duration of that impact are unmeasured.
input.executive_summary: An automated alert reported that the shop service was returning errors to its callers on the morning of 24 September 2026. Because none of the service's usage data could be read back during the investigation, we cannot say how many requests or customers were affected, how severe the error rate was, or how long the problem lasted — only that it began no later than the alert and had not been confirmed resolved by the end of the data we have. The automated responder picked up the alert immediately, attempted an investigation, found no data to work from, checked recent configuration changes and found none, and handed the incident to on-call engineers within roughly a minute. That handoff time describes how quickly we responded, not how long customers were affected. No fix was applied by automation, and no cause has been established. The most important follow-up is to find out why the service's metrics were unreadable, since that gap is what prevented any assessment of customer impact.
input.root_cause: Not determined. A HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop and the automated investigation returned no metrics at all for the incident window, so there is no evidence on which to base a cause; the flag provider showed no recent changes, which rules that out as a lead but does not point at anything else. The incident was escalated to humans for lack of evidence, and the service had not been observed to recover by the time the available metrics ended.
